merger_description:
VC Operations (WA) Pty Ltd (together with its associated entities, **Vets Central**) propose to acquire 100% of the business assets (both tangible and intangible) of Lava Street Veterinary Clinic and Doggy Kinder from Longyester Pty Ltd as trustee for the Longyester Unit Trust and Doggy Kinder Pty Ltd (the **Proposed Acquisition**).

Vets Central is an Australian-owned veterinary group that owns and operates 84 first opinion veterinary practices across Australia and New Zealand. In Australia, Vets Central’s practices provide core and ancillary veterinary services, for household pets as well as livestock, and other exotic species. The services primarily include routine, planned, and emergency veterinary services (excluding after-hours services).

Lava Street Veterinary Clinic and Doggy Kinder is full-service veterinary practice which also provides a dog daycare facility in the Warrnambool area of Victoria. The business provides a range of first opinion core and ancillary veterinary services for household pets (extending to exotic pets) in the local area.

determination_table_content.details:
VC Operations (WA) Pty Ltd (together with its associated entities,
Vets Central) applied for a notification waiver in respect of its
proposed acquisition of 100% of the business assets of Lava Street
Veterinary Clinic and Doggy Kinder from Longyester Pty Ltd as
trustee for the Longyester Unit Trust and Doggy Kinder Pty Ltd, as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Vets Central, is an Australian-owned veterinary group
that owns and operates 84 first opinion veterinary practices across
Australia and New Zealand. In Australia, Vets Central’s practices
provide core and ancillary veterinary services, for household pets as
well as livestock, and other exotic species. The services primarily
include routine, planned, and emergency veterinary services
(excluding after-hours services). Vets Central currently operates 9
veterinary clinics in Victoria.
The target, Lava Street Veterinary Clinic and Doggy Kinder, is a full-
service veterinary practice which also provides a dog daycare facility
in the Warrnambool area of Victoria. The business provides a range
of first opinion core and ancillary veterinary services for household
pets (extending to exotic pets) in the local area.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Vets Central and Lava
Street Veterinary Clinic and Doggy Kinder in the supply of
veterinary services in the Warrnambool area and a small
horizontal overlap by number of clinics in Victoria; and
b. there are alternative suppliers of veterinary services in the
Warrnambool area and more broadly at the state (Victoria)
and national level.

The ACCC has also had regard to the likelihood that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds
determined under section 51ABP(1) of the Act would apply.
While the ACCC considers that the notification thresholds are likely
to be met, given that material competition concerns are unlikely to
arise, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required
to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
